pf.license.insurance: liability insurance shown as 'insured' only once the owner sends the certificate
pf.license.away: training at the owner's home is allowed by trainers the owner clears for it
pf.license.renter: a trainer who rents the floor for their own classes is their own business: their own prices, terms and Stripe

stop.words: a bite or a dog fight happening now; someone badly hurt by a dog
stop.say: Call 911 if anyone is badly hurt. Keep the dogs apart from people and other pets.

stop.words: a dog that is very sick or hurt now (like after eating something)
stop.say: Call your vet now. Rosie gives no health advice.
stop.booking: no booking; the lesson can move with no fee

goOn.words: a bite earlier, with nobody badly hurt now
goOn.what: the safety steps first (keep the dog apart; see a doctor for the bite), then the booking goes on and waits for the owner's OK

goOn.words: a dog that growls, snaps or guards things
goOn.what: noted for the trainer on the secure page; a bite in its history sends the booking to the owner for an OK

pf.money.tax: a tax line for goods sold, like a long line, where the state's rules require it

pf.messages.minors: a junior handler's texts go to the parent or guardian

pf.staff.licenses: none for trainers or walkers; a certificate shows only once checked

pf.staff.supervision: none set in the example; an assistant trainer works only beside a trainer, where the owner sets it

pf.rules.bites: a bite report where the state's rules require one, made by the trainer or the owner, never by Rosie
pf.rules.advice: no diagnosis and no medicine advice: health questions go to the dog's vet, as the state's rules on vet practice require
pf.rules.vaccines: proof of rabies vaccination where the state's or the town's rules require it; the business's own rule for classes
pf.rules.contracts: a written package agreement or a cancel right for a package sold at the center or at the home, where the state's rules require it

notes:
Pilot: hair (from: hair). Dog training runs like a chair: a private lesson with a chosen trainer, booked by name, with the owner there, card saved for the late-cancel fee and paid at the front desk. The old flowchart's story is exactly that (a private lesson first for a dog that barks at other dogs). Group classes are the less usual part, so they use the master's own class branches (S2-32's timetable, A4-66's seat in a session, A7-67's minimum) instead of starting from yoga.
Usual side: flow A, the training center (the old flowchart's center, with private lessons and Saturday classes). Flow B is a trainer at the owner's home (the old flowchart's home lesson within 10 miles).
Names: Sam's main company is Lee Pet Services LLC (in-home training, with dog walking as its second kind of work; 215 River Rd); the second company is Lee Dog Training LLC (60 Mill St). Trade names: Lee In-Home Training and Lee Dog Walking. Trainers: Lauren and Dev at the center (the master's Riley and Avery); Marcus and Darius go to homes (Jordan and Casey, both 'he'). Dogs: Juno (A, 1-year-old shepherd mix) and Milo (B, 5-month-old puppy), each booked under its owner, Alex M. Alex's home: 9 Cedar Ct.
Prices at the center are changed from the master's barbershop numbers to dog training's own, with every sum kept: $35 to $120 (private lesson, 60 min), $20 to $60 (the fee, and 30 extra minutes), $55 to $180 (behavior evaluation, 90 min; 180 - 60 = 120 still holds), $40 to $135 (reactive dog lesson, and the raised lesson price), $25 to $70 (junior handler lesson), $75 to $150 (the center's lesson at home), $140 to $210 (the 6-week Manners class). They are the example's own prices, not a standard.
Prices at home keep the master's numbers: $179 in-home lesson, $89 late-cancel or no-show fee, $150 puppy start-up visit ($150 - $89 = $61 still holds), $199 home evaluation ($249 with Sam), $640 4-lesson package, $40 second dog.
Money paths: A lists list|card|counter (lessons) and list|full|none (evaluations and 6-week classes, paid up front). B lists list|card|bill (main: the bill with a tip line, as the old flowchart's pay link with a tip), list|card|card (the saved card at DONE) and list|full|none (puppy visits and packages). No holds, deposits, photo quotes or prices set at the visit: dog training prices every lesson from the list.
Packages and 6-week courses: the old flowchart sold them outside Rosie (an old single-sessions-only answer); the master now sells packs and series, so a 4-lesson package is bought paid in full and each lesson uses a credit (A5-03, A5-22, B5-01), and a 6-week class books all its weeks at once (A4-31, A8-41).
Sign-up: S1-12 to S1-17, S1-38, S1-39, S1-41, S1-42, S1-45 (paid in full), S1-47 and S1-57 have words ops with dog training's real money: card saved for the fee, paid at the front desk at the center; the bill at home; evaluations, classes, puppy visits and packages paid in full. No holds or deposits. Sam leaves bank transfer off (small bills).
Licenses: no state license for training or walking (S1-60 and S2-28 take the no-license branches); the center gives a kennel or facility license where the state's rules require one (S1-63, KN20981). A trainer's certificate (CPDT-KA) is a claim shown only once checked; S11-50 reminds about its renewal; S11-42's lapsed-license re-check is off.
Flow B starts at a set time (B4-84, 9:00am), never an arrival window; every window in the master's words becomes a start time, and the visit's clock runs OMW 8:40am, check-in 9:00am, DONE 10:00am, bill 10:02am, receipt 10:05am, homework 10:10am. Flow A's lesson runs 11:00am to 12:00pm (90 minutes for an evaluation), so the next booking and 'running late' times move to 12:00pm (12:30pm).
Own steps: A10-x01 and B10-x01 send the trainer's homework right after the receipt, on the main path. Also listed as a gap: tutors, coaches, music teachers and therapists send session notes too.
Bite history: A4-43's 'A reaction last time' branch becomes 'A bite in the dog's history' (A4-49): the booking waits for Sam's OK, who can OK it, offer the evaluation first, or ask for a vet visit first. A bite during a lesson (A8-38, B8-34): the lesson ends, an incident note, any report the state's rules require, and the next booking waits for Sam's OK.
Vaccines: rabies proof for any visit, DHPP and Bordetella for a group class (the example business's rule), uploaded on the secure page with the waiver (A4-72, B4-86), on file until each end date (A4-44). Missing at the visit: A8-02's 'Something required is missing' branch is kept (A8-51, B8-54).
Owner present: A8-53 and A8-67 keep the owner with the dog; B8-67, B8-69 and B8-70 keep 'Someone must be home'. Reactive dogs can check in from the car (A8-03 more), from the old flowchart's parking-lot check-in; listed as a gap too.
Off, as never used in dog training: holds and the day-before hold (A7-02), plan and insurance branches (A4-28, A4-54, A7-02, A9-15; B4-43, B4-63, B7-05, B9-19), items not picked up and rented items (A10-06, B10-07), a free fix and warranty claims (training promises no result), stays, drop-offs and spaces, sent now and live lines, a crew, dates that can't move, a damage hold, contracts, permits, notices, parts, deliveries, items to the shop, landlords, bank transfer, the color-quote OK (S11-08) and the emergency price checks (S12-20's higher-price branches: no quotes).
Shared what-ifs renamed to dog training: S11-56 switches a lesson from a card saved to paid in full (no hold or deposit), S11-58 adds grooming (center) and pet sitting (in-home), S11-40 is a talk about a dog's bite history, Morgan's plan is a monthly lesson for each of her two dogs, and Nora's and Lin's examples save a card instead of holding $89.
splitsKept: A: S2-32 (the center runs classes, the in-home company doesn't), A7-59, S11-87, S11-90 (lessons by name, classes not), A7-61 (an evaluation has no stand-in), A7-67 (classes have a minimum, lessons don't), A8-02 (vaccine proof can be missing). B: S2-32, S11-87, S11-90.
Old outside software (Square Appointments, Gingr, Square's own texts and reminders) is outdated: Rosie is the business's software. Old one-state facts (Connecticut's facility license, Iowa, a California code section) become switches in pf.license and pf.rules.
Not sure: the 24-hour and 7am cancel windows and the $60 and $89 fees are the example's settings; real trainers vary. Board-and-train stays are left out of the example (A4-66's stay branch is off); a trainer who offers them would turn the stay branch on.
Reviewer (Oct 23): flow A also lists list|card|bill, the old flowchart's pay link at checkout (Saturday mornings, when Lauren works alone, Rosie texts the bill with a tip line). The center sells its own 4-lesson package ($440) at the front desk, never in a booking text. Home evaluations are Marcus's or Sam's. Texts to Sam and staff carry no bite or incident details: only 'an incident' and 'the note is on the secure page'. Licenses show as none needed on every team screen.
